main_body: Tiled gabled roof (rows 0-53) with a half-timbered dormer, above a plaster and timber front wall with double barn doors (rows 54-90)
top_band: Large terracotta roof slope, orange/maroon scalloped tiles, rows 0-53 with a cream ridge highlight at rows 3-5; it ends in a lighter tile course at rows 49-51 before the dark eave
evidence: The roof is a big visible sloped surface, as in the Beodeul house references. Its lower edge is a lighter tile course at rows 49-51, followed by a dark eave shadow at rows 54-56 above the wall. The wall face below is vertical, with its own timber framing and plaster. Windows have dark frames and sills, and the doors have framed planks, so the front reads as inset rather than flat. The dormer sits on the roof with its own sill and shadow. No receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The roof has per-tile scallops in 4-5 steps (cream, light orange, orange, maroon, deep purple). The plaster has speckle dots, the wood has grain and diagonal braces, and the windows are detailed with a flower box. Outlines are dark brown or purple tinted to the neighbouring material, not neutral black. It is comparable in richness to the references, and its flat fills are small.
